anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet, the fan headers J7 and J8 are drawn as 4-pin connectors (Conn_01x04_Pin, pin 4 marked no-connect). The FAN_0_TACH / FAN_1_TACH signals are brought to pin 2 of J7/J8, while the +12V rail is wired to a different pin of each connector (pin 1 and/or pin 3) together with the D7 reverse-clamp diode.
anomalies.expected: The spec states that the 12 V pins of the fan headers are J7 pin 2 and J8 pin 2 ("the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)"); pin 2 should therefore sit on the +12V net, with the tach signal on the remaining signal pin (standard 4-pin fan wiring: 1=GND, 2=+12V, 3=Tach, 4=PWM/NC).

evidence.quote: Also on this net: ... and the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2).
Power sheet: J7 Conn_01x04_Pin with FAN_0_TACH on pin 2 and +12V on pin 1; J8 Conn_01x04_Pin with FAN_1_TACH on pin 2 and +12V on pin 1

anomalies.impact: The fans would not receive +12V on the pin the design expects; instead a logic-level tach signal is presented on the power pin and +12V is applied to a different pin, so the fans would not run correctly and the tach inputs would be mis-driven (potential damage to the fan and/or the ESP32 tach input).

parsed.summary: Most of the board matches the specification (ESP32-C3, three MAX31855 channels with shared SCK/SO and separate CS0-2, TPS2121 power mux, AP63203 buck, TPS1H200 heater switch, USB-C and WS2812B), but the fan headers J7/J8 appear to have the FAN_0_TACH/FAN_1_TACH signals on pin 2, the pin the spec designates as the +12V fan supply, so the fan interface is mis-wired.
